chunks: What al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me of, from Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa al-Tallaʿukbari, from Abu al-ʿAbbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saʿid Ibn ʿUqdah al-Hafiz, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Awdi; and Ahmad ibn ʿAbdun informed me, from Abu al-Hasan ʿAli ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Husayn ibn Nuʿaym al-Sahhaf, who said:
I said to Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: “A slave-mother of mine sees blood while she is pregnant; what should she do regarding salat?” He said, and said:

“If the pregnant woman sees blood after twenty days have passed from the time in which she used to see blood in the month in which she used to refrain, then that is not from the womb and not from menstruation; so she should perform wudu (ablution), insert cotton, and pray. But if the pregnant woman sees blood shortly before the time in which she used to see blood, or at that time in that month, then it is from menstruation; so she should refrain from salat for the number of her days during which she used to refrain in her menstruation. If the blood stops before that, then she should perform ghusl and pray. If the blood does not stop except after the days in which she used to see blood have passed by a day or two, then she should perform ghusl, insert cotton, bind herself, and pray al-zuhr and al-ʿasr. Then she should observe: if the blood, between that and al-maghrib, does not flow beyond the back of the cotton, then she should perform wudu (ablution) and pray at the time of each salat so long as she does not remove the cotton from herself. But if she removes the cotton from herself and the blood flows, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her.”
He said: “And if she removes the cotton from herself and the blood does not flow, then she should perform wudu (ablution) and pray, and no ghusl is upon her.”

He said: “And if the blood, when she holds the cotton, flows from behind the cotton in a steady stream and does not cease, then she must perform ghusl three times in every day and night, insert cotton, and pray: she performs ghusl for al-fajr, performs ghusl for al-zuhr and al-ʿasr, and performs ghusl for al-maghrib and al-ʿishaʾ al-akhirah.” He said: “And likewise the mustahadah does; for when she does that, Allah removes the blood from her.”

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman, central to determining the legal ruling
key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the noon salat, mentioned in the schedule of prayers and ghusl
key_terms.الْحَيْضَةِ: menstruation, which requires refraining from salat for the habitual number of days
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required in specified cases of continued or flowing blood
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفِ: cotton used to contain and check the flow of blood
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istihadah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding

ai.seo_question: What should a pregnant woman do about salat if she sees blood, and when is ghusl required?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for a pregnant woman who sees blood, distinguishing between blood treated as hayd and blood treated as istihadah based on timing and flow. It also details when wudu (ablution) is sufficient, when ghusl becomes obligatory, and how the mustahadah should manage her salat and ritual purity.
